mask_collision_pairs.ROI_definition: one-pixel dilation of the common largest connected v1 color-mask component; no true pose/ROI used

conclusions: Observed cal-T-10/cal-T-11 have identical binary fit inputs and identical decoded pose, opposite strict-success labels, but different complete RGB and RGB-derived object-boundary values.
Identical binary masks establish information loss in that chosen thresholding representation, not equality of complete RGB observations.
Nonzero RGB differences are not by themselves proof that a new decoder can recover pose/coverage reliably; that requires a frozen RGB-only algorithm and validation with failures retained.
The v1 object fit sees a binary object mask; subthreshold and antialias color differences never reach its silhouette objective.
Pusher segmentation/circularity and object-component/shape gates can reject generated frames independently of whether useful pose evidence survives in RGB.
True pose/contact/coverage and future actions may be error labels only; they must not select masks, ROI, initialization, angle neighborhood, candidate, or a successful fit.
Existing v1 calibration and main predictions have already been inspected. A reused-data v2 split is development evidence and must not be called an untouched final test.
component_method: Same 8-connectivity largest-component extraction as the source; no decoder fit or renderer invocation.
